overview_description.description:
Raisin is a savings and investment marketplace that connects retail customers with banks looking to expand deposit reach. The company's goal is to provide savers the best interest rates. The company gives access to exclusive savings products from all over Europe. Raisin assures a smooth investment process and the simple management of investments with all of the partner banks via one single platform.

Raisin was founded on 2012 and is headquartered in Berlin, Germany. Raisin DS was formed by a merger of the FinTech companies Deposit Solutions and Raisin in June 2021.

about_short_description.short_description: Raisin is a savings and investment marketplace that connects retail customers with banks looking to expand deposit reach.

product.name: Raisin Savings and Investment Marketplace
product.description: A digital marketplace that lets retail customers compare, open, and manage savings, deposit, and investment products from partner financial institutions through one account.

product.name: Savings Accounts
product.description: Variable-rate savings accounts that provide access to partner-bank interest offers while allowing customers to deposit and withdraw funds without a fixed maturity.

product.name: Term Deposits and Fixed-Term Savings
product.description: Fixed-rate deposit products that allow customers to invest money for a defined period in exchange for predictable interest payments.

product.name: Digital Wealth Management
product.description: An automated investment service that allocates customer money across globally diversified portfolios and performs ongoing portfolio monitoring and maintenance.

product.name: Raisin Retirement Products
product.description: Tax-advantaged retirement savings products, including Rürup and Riester pensions, designed for long-term retirement provision in the German market.

product.name: Flexgeld (Flexible Fixed-Term Deposits)
product.description: A deposit product combining a fixed rate and defined term with conditional early-access rights, typically applying a reduced base rate after early cancellation.
